purpose: Isolate whether increasing the IoT-23 per-scenario row cap from 100k to 300k improves the V29 clean-history unseen-family forecaster without changing its representation or global policy logic.
source: Official CTU IoT-23 timestamped Zeek conn.log.labeled scenarios
final_validation: locked; no final-validation family may be scored while V32 development is evaluated

data_change.all_other_temporal_rules: unchanged from V29/V30: 30-second windows, 8-minute clean history, 4-minute future, deterministic one-hour block split

feature_policy.representation: exact V29 causal topology, fanout, churn, concentration and periodicity summary

model.architecture: exact V29 balanced HistGradientBoosting supervised future-risk plus benign IsolationForest novelty branch
model.fusion_candidates: exact V29 fixed weight and policy-FPR grid
model.threshold: single global threshold selected from policy split only, exactly as V29; V30 scenario-specific thresholds are not used
model.event_denominator: V30 evaluable clean-onset events only; zero-candidate onsets are reported separately

isolation_interpretation: If V32 remains close to V29/V30 despite the 300k cap, row-cap expansion is not the main fix and subsequent work must target cross-scenario representation/calibration or better clean-onset data rather than more of the same rows.
claim_boundary: A pass supports these held-out development behaviours only. It does not establish universal zero-day or compromise prediction.
